title: Pontius Pilate
summary: Pontius Pilate governed Judea as prefect from 26 to 36 CE under Tiberius. An inscription found at Caesarea in 1961 confirms his title. Josephus reports clashes with Jewish subjects over Roman standards in Jerusalem and a temple-funded aqueduct, says he condemned Jesus to the cross, and records that Vitellius ordered him to Rome after Samaritan complaints.

uncertainty.note: The record covers his tenure as prefect; birth and death dates are not given on the opened pages. One page says he was summoned to Rome in 37 AD.

where.modern_name: Caesarea Maritima, Israel (where the Pilate inscription was found)
where.historical_name: Caesarea, seat of the Roman prefect of Judea

importance.justification: The Roman governor who, in Gospel and Josephus accounts, condemned Jesus; the Caesarea inscription is the main physical evidence of him.

sources.title: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, Book XVIII (Whiston translation)
sources.author: Flavius Josephus (trans. William Whiston)
